pathways.compact_statement: Repeated flooding may increase localized host-displaced tension when displacement concentrates people on scarce high ground with limited services and livelihood resources.
alternative_explanations: Conflict, poverty, service deficits, and pre-existing land disputes can independently drive displacement and host-community tension.
pathways.uncertainty: Localized pressure is documented; tension is neither universal nor primarily attributable to flooding.
recommendations: Retain only evidence whose documented geography supports the pathway location; otherwise narrow the pathway or keep the evidence standalone.

pathways.compact_statement: Climate-related livelihood and mobility changes may raise farmer-herder tension when customary route agreements and dispute-resolution arrangements are weak.
alternative_explanations: Political mobilization, cattle-raiding economies, weapons availability, and unresolved land claims can drive violence without a climate shock.
pathways.uncertainty: Mobility can support adaptation; tension depends on weak coordination and cannot be generalized.
recommendations: Retain only evidence whose documented geography supports the pathway location; otherwise narrow the pathway or keep the evidence standalone.
